messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: R interface via Rcpp
parts:
I finally understand how we can use "Rcpp package" to
build an R interface for Stan. Rcpp's much more
powerful than I first thought, though the documentation
is spread over several fragmentary pdfs.

Package: Stan
----

This is going to involve one basic function, stan(),
playing the role of bugs() in R2WinBUGS. The
signature is going to be something like:

StanSamples

stan(model,data,inits,
iter,warmup,thin,
... NUTS or HMC params ...,
... misc. params ...)


This will have to do a number of things which can be broken
out as sub-functions:

a. If the model hasn't been compiled, compile it using
the stanc compiler (what's now in demo/gm). We can
call the compiler from R using Rcpp.

b. If not already done, generate boilerplate around
the generated C++ model code to link it up with
Stan C++ to create a model-specific Rcpp package on the
fly.

c. Dynamically (re)link the newly created package, which
corresponds to the model.

d. Run the sampler (perhaps in multiple threads), and
save the results to a Coda-like C++ object which we make available
to R through Rcpp.

What's neat is that the implementation of (d) in C++
rather than in R means we can make Stan scalable beyond
what we could do if we had a Coda-like object in R.
Only the data that's being used need be brought into an R
representation. Of course, if you wind up bringing it all
in at once, that'll be less efficient, because now we have
all the R baggage and the C++ object.

It'll also mean no huge lag after sampling's done while all the
data gets marshaled in R.

This does mean we'd write things like ESS and WAIC
and split-R-hat in C++. This should make them faster.
And more portable (looks like the Rcpp package functionality
was based on Boost.Python, so maybe Python will be easy to
knock off next if all the heavy lifting (other than plotting)
is on the C++ side).

What I'd like to get some help with (Ben? Jiqiang? Malecki?)
is

1. setting up the R package boilerplate and figuring out where
everything needs to go like C++ compiler options and linked
libraries for Rcpp, and

2. writing the plotting commands in R and working with Andrew
to make them acceptable. There are three pieces to this, I think.
The basic plot() to summarize all the resulting posterior intervals
(edited to fit on one plot) and R-hat/ESS values, posterior plots
for individual or paired variables, and traceplots per variable (or
for pairs?).

- Bob

I would guess that it is easier to call the stanc compiler from R
rather than from Rcpp. The inline R package is intended to compile and
link code, so we could use or copy that.

> What I'd like to get some help with (Ben?  Jiqiang?  Malecki?)
> is
>
> 1.  setting up the R package boilerplate and figuring out where
> everything needs to go like C++ compiler options and linked
> libraries for Rcpp, and

What is currently in stan/rstan/rstan covers most of the boilerplate.
It was created by someone using Rcpp.package.skeleton(). In
particular, there are Makevars and Makevars.win files in stan/rstan/
rstan/src, in stan/rstan/rstan/src-i386, and in stan/rstan/rstan/src-
x86-64 that are used for C++ compiler options as documented at

http://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/R-exts.html#Using-Makevars

Ben

The stanc compiler is a C++ program that converts
the text file Stan model to another text file containing
C++. No C++ compilation or linking required here.

When we need to compile/link the generated C++ code,
the Rcpp package approach seems neat. The trick is
going to be using something that can dynamically link
and later re-link when the user changes the model.

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: naming
parts:
Just a request that we name the R package stan, not rstan or Rstan or whatever. I think this will be easier for people to remember. Also, we will want a print.stan as well as a plot.stan function. But print.stan should be simple enough: mean, sd, some quantiles, split R-hat, and ess, perhaps all rounded to a default of 2 decimal places.
A

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] naming
parts:
Yes, the plan is to call it Stan, not RStan.
I like the capitalization, which shows it's
a name in English.

Yes, we'll have print and plot functions.
And all the accessors you talked about in terms
of structured variables. And all the MCMC
convergence stuff, WAIC, and ESS.

I'm less sure about including methods for
means, quantiles, sd, etc. -- those should probably
just be run on the structured variables using
the standard R functions.

- Bob
